title: Roadmap list at height 10 cannot scroll up to the Goals block above the first row

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
At height 10 the Roadmap list shows the Goals block above the first row as `+5 lines above`, and no key reaches those lines. The page keys move the row cursor (`moveRows` in `internal/tui/model.go`), and the first row is already on screen, so `pgup`, `up` and `home` on that row do nothing. The scroll sweep (S531, adj 570) found this, and `internal/tui/scroll_sweep_test.go` leaves the height-10 case out until this slice lands.

Owner decision (adj 578, key `ui.roadmap-list-goals-scroll`, "pgup at top"): with the cursor on the first row, `pgup`, `up` and `home` scroll the hidden Goals lines into view. This slice does that and puts height 10 back in the sweep's `roadmap-list` case.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-25: adj 578 (pgup, up and home on the first row scroll the hidden Goals into view) and adj 582 (down, pgdown, G, { and } move the cursor as today and the window follows it, which ends the lift).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/tui/model.go:1174-1223` (`moveRows`: `pgup` and `home` on the first row lift the window; every other row key drops the lift)
- `internal/tui/model.go:1038-1042` (the `RowPrev` case: `up` on the first row lifts the window by a line)
- `internal/tui/model.go:161` (a new `roadmapLift` field beside `roadmapCursor`)
- `internal/tui/view.go:399-402` (`drawnRows` gains the body's total line count and window height, so the keys can size a page)
- `internal/tui/view.go:321-339` (the draw applies the lift to `start`, clamps it and drops it when the cursor has moved)
- `internal/tui/scroll_sweep_test.go:216-238` (add height 10 to `roadmap-list`; delete the S580 bullet from the `TestScrollSweep` comment)
- `internal/tui/roadmap_test.go` (new tests)
- `docs/dashboard.md:2025` (the Roadmap section: say how `pgup`, `up` and `home` reach the Goals)

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestScrollSweep/roadmap-list/h10 (`internal/tui/scroll_sweep_test.go`): with `heights` extended to `{10, 16, 24, 40}`, paging up from the last row to the first and then on must show every Goals line. It fails today with the Goals lines never shown.
- TestRoadmapPageUpAtTopScrollsGoalsIntoView (`internal/tui/roadmap_test.go`, new): at 80x10 with six goal records, cursor on row 0, the frame shows `+N lines above` and not the first goal. Each `pgup` shows earlier Goals lines while `roadmapCursor` stays 0. After enough presses the `Goals` heading is shown and no `lines above` marker is. One more `pgup` changes nothing.
- TestRoadmapUpAtTopScrollsOneLine (new): each `up` on row 0 reduces the `lines above` count by 1 and the cursor stays 0. At the top further presses change nothing.
- TestRoadmapHomeScrollsToGoalsOnlyFromTheFirstRow (new): `home` on row 3 moves the cursor to 0 and does not lift the window. A second `home` on row 0 shows the top of the body, `Goals` heading included.
- TestRoadmapGoalsLiftDropsWhenTheCursorMoves (new): after a lift, `G` puts the cursor on the last row and that row is on screen. Pressing `pgup` again from the first row lifts again.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/tui/view.go`, add `total, n int` to `drawnRows` (the body's line count and the window height). Set them where `m.drawn` is set at line 352.
2. In `internal/tui/model.go`, add `roadmapLift struct{ cursor, lines int }` to `Model`. `lines` is how many lines the Roadmap list's window starts above the one that follows the cursor, and `cursor` is the row it was set for.
3. In `internal/tui/view.go`, after the `pageTop` block (line 339) and before the help override, when `m.view == roadmapView && m.itemPane == nil && m.launch == nil`, apply the lift:
   - If `m.roadmapLift.cursor != clampCursor(m.roadmapCursor, len(m.roadmapItems()))`, zero `m.roadmapLift`.
   - Set `lines = min(lines, start)`.
   - Set `start -= lines`.
   The window then shows `+N lines above` and may drop the cursor row below its end. That is how the Goals lines come into view.
4. In `internal/tui/model.go`, add `liftRoadmap(step int)`. It calls `m.screen()` to refresh `m.drawn`. It sets `m.roadmapLift = {cursor: 0, lines: lines + min(step, m.drawn.lo)}`. `m.drawn.lo` is the start of the window as drawn, so the lift cannot pass the first body line.
5. In `moveRows`, clear `m.roadmapLift` for every key. Then, when the view is the Roadmap list (`m.itemPane == nil`, `m.launch == nil`), `at == 0` and `next == 0`:
   - `PageUp` calls `liftRoadmap` with one page, the step that makes the current window's first line the last line of the new one (the same search `scrollHelp` makes for `pgup`, over `m.drawn.total` and `m.drawn.n`).
   - `First` calls `liftRoadmap` with `m.drawn.lo`, so the window reaches the top.
   A `pgup` or `home` that moves the cursor off a later row is unchanged and lifts nothing.
6. In the `RowPrev` case (model.go:1038), when the Roadmap list is shown, the cursor is on row 0 and the list is not empty, call `liftRoadmap(1)`. Any other `RowNext` or `RowPrev` that moves the cursor leaves `roadmapLift` for step 3 to drop.
7. In `internal/tui/scroll_sweep_test.go`, set the `roadmap-list` heights to `sweepAll` and remove the S580 bullet from the comment above `TestScrollSweep`.
8. Add the four new tests to `internal/tui/roadmap_test.go`. Build the goals from `roadmapHarness`'s snapshot with extra `Goals.Value.Records.Goal` entries, and size the window with `tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 80, Height: 10}`.
9. In `docs/dashboard.md` at line 2025 (the Roadmap section), add one or two sentences: on the first row `pgup` and `up` scroll the Goals into view by a page and by a line, and `home` scrolls to the top. State the way back as the owner decides it (see Owner needed).
10. Run `slicer changelog add S580 --text "Roadmap list: pgup, up and home on the first row scroll the hidden Goals lines into view (adj 578)"` (adj 402, 404, 445). Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Acceptance: on the Roadmap list at 80x10, with the cursor on the first row, pgup, up and home bring the Goals block into view. pgup or home from a later row still moves the cursor as before.
- `go test ./internal/tui -run 'TestScrollSweep/roadmap-list' -v` passes with roadmap-list/h10 among the passing subtests.
- `go test ./internal/tui -run 'TestRoadmapPageUpAtTopScrollsGoalsIntoView|TestRoadmapUpAtTopScrollsOneLine|TestRoadmapHomeScrollsToGoalsOnlyFromTheFirstRow|TestRoadmapGoalsLiftDropsWhenTheCursorMoves' -v` passes, and each test fails when the lift is removed.
- `go test ./...` exits 0. TestPageKeysMoveRowsWithoutAPane, TestGroupKeysOnTheRoadmapJumpBetweenPasses, TestRoadmapItemPaneScrollsByLinePageAndEnds and the golden tests are unchanged.
- `go vet ./...` prints nothing.
- `gofmt -l ./tui` prints nothing.
- `slicer check --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork` reports no problem.
- [HUMAN CHECK] Run ork in a terminal of 80x10, open a project's Roadmap with several goals and press pgup on the first row. The Goals lines should scroll into view and +N lines above should count down to the Goals heading. Then press down: the cursor should reach the second row and its row should be on screen.
